_comment: Every fact about the business lives in this one file. Change it here and it
changes everywhere on the site — page copy, the footer, the phone links, and
the structured data Google reads.
TWO DELIBERATE OMISSIONS, so they do not get written back in by accident:
1. The Montauk Hwy showroom is small, so the site does not invite visits or
lead with it. The address stays listed because Google cross-checks it
against the Business Profile — but nothing says 'stop by'.
2. The Fanning Ave slab shop is not mentioned anywhere, by choice. It is
not off limits to customers, but they are not being pointed there.
3. No job timelines anywhere. Every job differs and the season drives both
schedule and price, so time and cost are settled in the estimate.
The contact details below were taken from the business's public listings
(Yelp, Yahoo Local, Angi, Experience.com, hub.biz) in August 2026. Check them
against what your uncle actually says before launch — directories go stale.
Anything still starting with 'TODO:' is unfilled; `npm run build` lists them.
url is the ORIGIN only (no path). basePath is the subfolder the site is
served from. On GitHub Pages under a repo name, basePath is that repo name.
When a real domain is connected: url = https://stylemarbleandtile.com and
basePath = "".

_technology_note: Specs are from the shop's own August 2024 post. The 'first in the country' claim is deliberately tied to when the machine was installed, because it will not stay true forever.

technology.title: The machine that cuts your stone
technology.blurb: In 2024 we brought in a dual-router CNC and saw from Construal — the first of its kind in the country at the time. It is not there to be impressive. It is there because it changes what we can promise you about your own slab.

points.title: We plan the layout on your actual slab
points.body: An overhead camera scans the slab, so the cuts are laid out on the real veining rather than on a generic rectangle. That is how the veins line up across a seam, around a mitre, and up onto a shower ceiling — you can see where the figure will fall before anything is cut.

points.title: Blocks up to 12 inches thick
points.body: Not just slabs. Thick blocks, which is what carved basins, solid mitred edges, and one-piece steps and hearths are cut from.

points.title: Suction arms move the stone
points.body: Slabs get lifted flat instead of manhandled. Less flex, fewer cracks, and a safer shop.

points.title: Oversized on purpose
points.body: Twenty-eight feet long by eighteen wide, and twelve feet to the top of the saw motor. Big pieces do not have to be cut down just to fit the machine, so long runs stay in one piece.

differentiators.title: We fabricate it ourselves
differentiators.body: Templating, fabrication, and installation are all in house, on our own CNC. Nothing gets lost in a handoff between a fabricator and an installer who have never met, and if something needs adjusting on install day, the people who cut it are standing there.

differentiators.title: Working the East End since 1987
differentiators.body: Nearly four decades of stone on this end of the island. We know which materials hold up in a house that sits empty half the winter and gets hammered all summer, and which ones only look good for two years — and we will tell you which is which before you buy.

differentiators.title: The hand work still gets done by hand
differentiators.body: Most of a countertop is machine work, and that is fine — machines are accurate. But the delicate custom trim pieces get cut by hand, because that is the only way they come out right.

differentiators.title: Licensed, insured, and permitted
differentiators.body: Fully licensed and insured, and permitted in every local municipality we work in. Out here that matters more than most places — village and town codes on the East End are strict, and a contractor who is not permitted where you live can stall a job for weeks.

faq.a: We are based in Hampton Bays and work across the South Fork and North Fork — Southampton, Westhampton, Quogue, Bridgehampton, Sag Harbor, East Hampton, Montauk, Riverhead, and the surrounding hamlets. If your town is not on that list, call and ask.

faq.q: Do you sell tile, or only install it?
faq.a: Both. We supply the tile as well as installing it, so you can buy the material from us and have us set it.

faq.q: What is the difference between marble, quartzite, and quartz?
faq.a: Marble is natural stone that etches with acid and patinas over time — beautiful, but it asks something of you. Quartzite is natural and much harder, so it resists etching and scratching. Quartz is engineered and non-porous, which makes it the lowest-maintenance of the three. We will walk you through the tradeoffs for how you actually use your kitchen.

faq.q: How long will my job take, and what will it cost?
faq.a: Every job is different, and the time of year makes a real difference out here — the season the East End runs on affects both scheduling and pricing. Rather than quote a number we cannot stand behind, we work out the time and the cost together with you as part of the estimate, once we have seen the job.

faq.q: My marble is etched and dull in places. Can that be fixed?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Etching is acid damage to the surface — rings from a glass, a lemon left on the counter — and it is not a stain you can scrub out, it is the polish eaten away. We can restore the surface and then seal it with MORE AntiEtch so it does not keep happening. You do not need to have bought the tops from us.

faq.q: What is AntiEtch, and do I need it?
faq.a: MORE AntiEtch is an invisible sealer that defends marble against acids and staining — the wine, lemon, vinegar and cleaning products that dull a polished top. We are certified applicators. If you have marble in a kitchen you actually cook in, it is worth asking about; on quartz or granite it is usually not necessary, and we will tell you so.
Yes — fully licensed and insured, and permitted in every local municipality we work in. If your village or town needs paperwork filed before work starts, that is handled.

_comment: IMPORTANT: only REAL reviews, copied verbatim, with the reviewer's real
name. Do not write testimonials and do not tidy up the ones below. Fake or
materially altered reviews are illegal under the FTC's rule on consumer
reviews (16 CFR Part 465).
Quoted exactly as posted, typos included — 'Grate people' is Nirit's, not a
mistake here. Fixing a reviewer's spelling means publishing words they did
not write, and the small gain is not worth it.
Dates: Yelp and Google only showed 'N years ago' when these were captured
in August 2026, so most are year-only. Ellen signed hers with a month.
NOTE ON STARS IN SEARCH: these feed the aggregateRating in the page's
structured data, but Google does not show star rich results for reviews a
business hosts about itself (self-serving markup, LocalBusiness types). The
stars people see next to the business in search come from the Google
Business Profile. The markup still gets read and can inform AI summaries,
so it stays — just do not expect it to put stars on the search page.

items.author: Ellen H.
items.text: I just completed the most fantastic, painless and seamless "update" to my kitchen with Style Marble. After much debate, I "finally" got rid of the countertop granite circa (very long ago!) and went to Silestone. My experience with the owner / Melissa / Raul (sp?) and the rest of the team was 10/10. I found each of them to be courteous, professional and the quality of their workmanship and installation was, in a word, fantastic! I can't say enough great things about Style Marble.

items.author: Debbie C.
items.text: I'm so glad my contractor found this company. They have been terrific. We ordered 2 slabs - one was a quartz stone and one was a granite stone. The granite we needed had to match our current granite stone, which was installed 15 years ago and had to be the same color. Not every place could find the match. Style Marble did and the stone top came out perfectly. i actually went to their location to pick out where i wanted the quartz to be cut and the staff was terrific. The installation was perfect as well. i highly recommend this company.

items.author: Barbara T.
items.text: Style did a great job, helped me pick the right material for the counter top in kitchen, came to measure really quickly, created and installed a really nice counter for the sink area in the kitchen. I would work with them any time. They were friendly, helpful, and efficient!
